<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917181_theRebbe_116" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917181_theRebbe_116__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B"S.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Mishpatim,</t>
    <t s="2">Parshas Shekalim,</t>
    <t s="3">Rosh Chodesh Adar, 5740*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the verses about the half-shekel, its connection to the sin of the Golden Calf, and its parallel in prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"This they shall give, everyone who passes among those counted, a half-shekel of the holy shekel—twenty gerahs the shekel—a half-shekel as an offering to Hashem..."1</t>
    <t s="1">And it concludes2</t>
    <t s="2">"to make atonement for your souls."</t>
    <t s="3">And the maamar of Shabbos Parshas Mishpatim and Parshas Shekalim 5680</t>
    <t s="4">(printed in Pardes)3</t>
    <t s="5">questions the double expression of "half-shekel" in the verse,</t>
    <t s="6">which says "a half-shekel of the holy shekel,"</t>
    <t s="7">and then repeats "a half-shekel as an offering to Hashem."</t>
    <t s="8">Also, what is the meaning of "twenty gerahs the shekel,"</t>
    <t s="9">since one only needs to give a half-shekel?</t>
    <t s="10">It also questions the meaning of "to make atonement for your souls,"</t>
    <t s="11">and as it continues and explains there that the concept of the half-shekel is to atone for the sin of the Golden Calf4,</t>
    <t s="12">and it questions what is the virtue of the half-shekel that it is so capable of atoning for that sin.</t>
    <t s="13">And one may add to this</t>
    <t s="14">(as a comment in brief),</t>
    <t s="15">that the sin of the Golden Calf is a general sin, and it is the source and root of all sins, iniquities, and transgressions.</t>
    <t s="16">And as it is brought in the Gemara5</t>
    <t s="17">that at the time of the Giving of the Torah, their contamination ceased</t>
    <t s="18">(that the serpent had injected into Chavah),</t>
    <t s="19">and after the sin of the Golden Calf it returned6.</t>
    <t s="20">And although it did not return completely as it was before that7,</t>
    <t s="21">for even after the sin of the Golden Calf the concept of choice remained for the Jewish people,</t>
    <t s="22">"and in us You chose"8,</t>
    <t s="23">in the physical body which in its materiality resembles the bodies of the nations of the world9</t>
    <t s="24">(and see in the Gemara there10</t>
    <t s="25">"Why are the nations of the world contaminated..."),</t>
    <t s="26">nevertheless, the sin of the Golden Calf is the general sin,</t>
    <t s="27">and about it is written11</t>
    <t s="28">"And on the day I make My account"</t>
    <t s="29">(for every sin)</t>
    <t s="30">"I shall bring it to account..."</t>
    <t s="31">Therefore, an explanation is most needed as to what is the virtue of the half-shekel that atones for this sin.</t>
    <t s="32">And now, from this offering</t>
    <t s="33">(of the half-shekel)</t>
    <t s="34">they purchased the communal offerings for the entire year,</t>
    <t s="35">and the concept of offerings nowadays is the concept of prayer,</t>
    <t s="36">as our sages, of blessed memory, said12</t>
    <t s="37">"Prayers were instituted in place of the offerings,"</t>
    <t s="38">and from this it is understood</t>
    <t s="39">that the concept of the half-shekel also exists in the service of prayer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the concept of prayer as being from a "heavy head," referring to the deficiency in the Shechinah and in the souls of Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand all this, the maamar continues to explain13</t>
    <t s="2">the concept of prayer,</t>
    <t s="3">and brings on this the statement of our sages, of blessed memory14</t>
    <t s="4">"One should not stand to pray except from a heavy head."</t>
    <t s="5">And one may add to this,</t>
    <t s="6">based on what Tosafos says in Maseches Menachos15</t>
    <t s="7">that the language "one should not... except..." comes to exclude, meaning it is invalid after the fact.</t>
    <t s="8">And so is the simple explanation of the matter,</t>
    <t s="9">that "one should not stand to pray,"</t>
    <t s="10">meaning that the concept of prayer does not apply,</t>
    <t s="11">except from a heavy head.</t>
    <t s="12">And it brings on this the explanation of the Maggid of Mezeritch, his soul in Eden16</t>
    <t s="13">that the prayer should be about the heaviness in the head,</t>
    <t s="14">that when one prays about a deficiency, he should not pray about his own deficiency, but about the deficiency above,</t>
    <t s="15">for there is no deficiency below that does not have a deficiency above.</t>
    <t s="16">And he explains,</t>
    <t s="17">that the concept of the deficiency above is as our sages, of blessed memory, said17</t>
    <t s="18">"At a time when a person is distressed, what does the Shechinah say? As it were, 'My head is heavy upon Me, My arm is heavy upon Me,'"</t>
    <t s="19">for the Shechinah is the aspect of Malchus, which has ascents and descents, etc.</t>
    <t s="20">And this is the concept of the "heavy head" of the Shechinah,</t>
    <t s="21">and this is "one should not stand to pray except from a heavy head,"</t>
    <t s="22">meaning, about the heaviness and deficiency in the head.</t>
    <t s="23">And afterwards it brings the explanation of our master, the Alter Rebbe</t>
    <t s="24">(and so it is also in the discourse "Ein Omdin Lehispael" of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe18)</t>
    <t s="25">that "head" refers to the souls of Israel.</t>
    <t s="26">"Israel is the head for Me,"</t>
    <t s="27">and in this there is the concept of "heavy head" caused by sins,</t>
    <t s="28">as it is written19</t>
    <t s="29">"For my iniquities have passed over my head; like a heavy burden, they are too heavy for me."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
